name: Gone with the Wind
hook: The American novel Jeopardy asks about more than any other. Six things cover almost every clue.

facts.label: Margaret Mitchell
facts.statement: Margaret Mitchell wrote it — her only novel, published in 1936, and winner of the 1937 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

facts.label: Scarlett O'Hara
facts.statement: Scarlett O'Hara is the heroine. The novel opens by saying she "was not beautiful," and her last line is "After all, tomorrow is another day."

facts.label: Rhett Butler
facts.statement: Rhett Butler is the male lead — Clark Gable in the film — and speaks the famous last line about not giving a damn.

facts.label: Tara
facts.statement: Tara is the O'Hara family plantation. Twelve Oaks belongs to the Wilkes family.

facts.label: the 1939 film
facts.statement: The 1939 film starred Vivien Leigh as Scarlett and Clark Gable as Rhett. Victor Fleming directed it — and The Wizard of Oz in the same year.

facts.label: Hattie McDaniel
facts.statement: Hattie McDaniel played Mammy and became the first African-American performer to win an Oscar.

facts.label: Atlanta, Georgia
facts.statement: It is set in Atlanta and rural Georgia during the Civil War and Reconstruction. The 1939 premiere was in Atlanta on December 15.
